claims: You can build and launch a full mobile app to the App Store with zero coding skills
React Native + Expo is 'by far the fastest stack' for iOS and Android from one codebase
Claude can write the title, description and 'certificates' for submission
how_to_steps: Ask Claude to install React Native and Expo in the terminal
Build the most basic MVP, then add features and 'reactivation loop' hooks that bring people back
Test in Chrome, then scan the Expo QR code to run on your phone
Ask Claude to write the App Store title, description and handle certificates
Use a Claude skill (/mockup-app-skill) to generate the App Store screenshot set
Submit for review; publish once approved
on_screen_only: 'BUILD APPS WITH CLAUDE [No coding skills required]' with Claude Code and OpenRouter logos
Terminal: 'Installing React Native & Expo - $ npx create-expo-app my-app - react-native installed - expo installed - Done - ready to run!'; 'npm run ios', 'npm run android'
'/mockup-app-skill' with CalTracker phone mockup; 'Publish CalTracker' form; 'App Store Review - Approved by Apple'
Stock footage of a 'Vue 101 - Getting Started With Vue - LevelUpTuts' YouTube video (unrelated)

relevance.why: Haji builds apps; a mobile shipping path matters, but this is surface-level and skips the painful parts (Apple developer account, EAS build, provisioning, review rejections).

implement_score.why: The stack choice (Expo) is sound and the screenshot-skill idea is handy, but the skill is unnamed and nothing here saves real time versus Expo's own docs. Worth a note, not a project.

gap.what: Liked set has no mobile/App Store pipeline at all; adds Expo-with-Claude-Code as the stack and the idea of a skill that generates App Store screenshot sets.

verify: Which skill is '/mockup-app-skill' (repo?) and does it output Apple-compliant screenshot sizes?
'Certificates' cannot be written by Claude; needs Apple Developer account + EAS/Xcode signing
Is OpenRouter actually part of the workflow or just a logo?
